name: Sweden
sources: GDP: nominal SEK 1,443bn in 1990 at the year-average 5.92 SEK/USD gives about $245bn (SCB national accounts). Population 8.56m (SCB, 1990).
Inflation 10.4% (SCB consumer price index, 1990) - the peak of the overheating that ended in the 1992 krona crisis. Riksbank marginal lending near 12.5%.
Tax revenue 52% of GDP (OECD Revenue Statistics, 1990), the highest in the OECD that year.
Central government debt about 42% of GDP in 1990, before the banking crisis roughly doubled it.

Defence 2.6% of GDP. Strength 14 rather than the 8-9 a $245bn economy would otherwise buy: armed neutrality with universal conscription, a wartime mobilisation strength above 700,000, and a domestic combat-aircraft industry (Viggen in service, Gripen in flight test).
Sweden was outside NATO and outside the EC in 1990; its EC application went in during July 1991.
